questions.q: How many branches does the U.S. federal government have?
questions.why: Legislative (makes laws), executive (carries them out) and judicial (interprets them).

questions.q: Which branch writes and passes laws?
questions.why: Legislatures, like Congress or a state legislature, write and pass laws.

questions.q: What is it called when a president or governor rejects a bill?
questions.why: The bill goes back to lawmakers, who can sometimes override it.

questions.q: How much of Congress is needed to override a presidential veto?
questions.why: Two-thirds of both the House and the Senate.

questions.q: What is the minimum voting age in U.S. federal elections?
questions.why: The 26th Amendment, ratified in 1971, set it at 18.

choices: The minimum number of members who must be present to do business

questions.why: Without a quorum, a legislature or board can't take official action.

questions.q: What does a primary election usually decide?
choices: Which candidate represents a party in the general election
questions.why: Primaries pick each party's nominee; the general election picks the winner.

questions.q: At many city council meetings, residents speak during a set time. What is it usually called?
questions.why: Public comment lets anyone address officials, often for two or three minutes.
